g.text: matrix scan -> host: resends, timeouts, stalled-link teardown
nothing waits on a peer forever:
every wait on a link ends in a timeout
send error while the right half is up
-> resend flag (lost pointer deltas stay lost)
send error while the right half is up
-> KeyScanner_ResendKeyStates, resent on the next scan
link reset -> full key state resend
send error -> property marked dirty again
a failed send leaves its data marked for resend
Messenger_Send2: no retry of its own,
state sync sends fail; typed keys must still arrive
NUS server slots are shared by all dongle links:
with two dongles, the wrong one may be cut
one report in flight per type
send: sink, connection and time noted,
in flight blocks sending: up to 32 ms
baseline kept, resend with backoff 1..32 ms
late callback (not in flight, or other sink) ignored
the baseline advances only on confirmed delivery;
late callbacks must not release a newer report
12 failed tries -> given up: reports go out unconfirmed,
state resent after 1 s; may reconnect the host
given up: a lost report is repaired
[Zephyr] one ATT TX pool for all BLE links
per-sender caps: HID 3 (one per report type)
each sender caps its in-flight PDUs;
the caps together fit in the shared pool
allocation never blocks, senders retry on their own
fallback only if the report exceeds the MTU
[radio] HCI send credits (3) are shared too,
shared HCI send credits: a NUS timeout may cut
a healthy link while a HOGP stall clears
why: a stalled link plus 32 ms resends once filled the pool
and blocked the sender forever (a 55 s freeze)
an accepted report is never resent,
BLE delivers in order, or the link goes down
(always ok; none if the link drops)
peer radio up, its BT stack not taking data
or no NUS send slot within 1 s
a link that stops taking data
is torn down, and only that link
link down frees its buffers; the reset resends
key states and state sync properties
[Zephyr patch] released ATT channel clears TX metadata:
no use-after-free when buffers outlive the link
same semaphore: waits for the callback;
resends on error or after 32 ms
